summary: Expands patient satisfaction survey coverage from ~521 records (1 in 160 orders) to ~8,300 records (1 in 10 orders) with realistic correlated ratings and varied feedback.

import random
from datetime import timedelta

# Fetch all order_id values and existing survey order_ids
cur.execute("SELECT order_id, order_date, customer_name, product_name FROM demo.orders ORDER BY order_id")
all_orders = cur.fetchall()

cur.execute("SELECT order_id FROM demo.patient_satisfaction")
existing_survey_orders = {row[0] for row in cur.fetchall()}

# Target: ~1 in 10 orders should have surveys (currently ~521, aiming for ~8,300)
target_count = len(all_orders) // 10
orders_to_survey = []

for order_id, order_date, customer_name, product_name in all_orders:
    if order_id not in existing_survey_orders and len(orders_to_survey) < target_count - len(existing_survey_orders):
        orders_to_survey.append((order_id, order_date, customer_name, product_name))

# Shuffle to avoid sequential bias
random.shuffle(orders_to_survey)

# Survey methods with realistic distribution
survey_methods = ['Email', 'Portal', 'SMS', 'Phone']
survey_method_weights = [0.40, 0.35, 0.20, 0.05]

# Feedback templates for different satisfaction levels
positive_feedback = [
    "Outstanding service. Dr. {name} took time to answer all my questions. {aspect} was seamless and efficient.",
    "Excellent care provided by Dr. {name}. Very impressed with the professionalism. {aspect} exceeded expectations.",
    "Exceptional experience. Dr. {name} was thorough and caring. Would highly recommend to family and friends.",
    "Very satisfied with my visit. Dr. {name} explained everything clearly. {aspect} made the process easy.",
    None, None  # 2 in 6 chance of no feedback even when satisfied
]

neutral_feedback = [
    "Fair experience. Dr. {name} was adequate but not exceptional. {aspect} was frustrating.",
    "Average service overall. Dr. {name} seemed rushed. {aspect} could be improved significantly.",
    None, None, None  # 3 in 5 chance of no feedback for neutral
]

negative_feedback = [
    "Disappointed with the care received. Dr. {name} didn't listen to my concerns. {aspect} was poorly handled.",
    "Poor experience. Long wait times and Dr. {name} seemed distracted. {aspect} needs major improvement.",
    "Unsatisfied with service quality. Dr. {name} was dismissive. Would not recommend based on this visit.",
    None, None  # 2 in 5 chance of no feedback even when negative
]

aspects = [
    "Scheduling process",
    "Check-in procedure",
    "Facility environment",
    "Follow-up communication",
    "Billing process"
]

# Generate survey IDs starting after existing max
cur.execute("SELECT MAX(SUBSTRING(survey_id FROM '[0-9]+$')::integer) FROM demo.patient_satisfaction")
max_id = cur.fetchone()[0] or 0

new_surveys = []

for idx, (order_id, order_date, customer_name, product_name) in enumerate(orders_to_survey, start=1):
    survey_id = f"SURV{str(max_id + idx).zfill(7)}"
    
    # Survey date: 1-14 days after order date
    survey_date = order_date + timedelta(days=random.randint(1, 14))
    
    # Generate correlated ratings
    # Start with base satisfaction (weighted toward positive)
    overall_satisfaction = random.choices([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], weights=[0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.35, 0.25])[0]
    
    # Appointment scheduling ease strongly correlates with overall (correlation ~0.7)
    if overall_satisfaction >= 4:
        appointment_scheduling_ease = random.choices([3, 4, 5], weights=[0.15, 0.40, 0.45])[0]
    elif overall_satisfaction == 3:
        appointment_scheduling_ease = random.choices([2, 3, 4], weights=[0.25, 0.50, 0.25])[0]
    else:
        appointment_scheduling_ease = random.choices([1, 2, 3], weights=[0.40, 0.45, 0.15])[0]
    
    # Other ratings correlate moderately with overall (correlation ~0.4-0.6)
    def correlated_rating(base, correlation_strength=0.5):
        if random.random() < correlation_strength:
            # Strong correlation: stay within ±1 of base
            return max(1, min(5, base + random.randint(-1, 1)))
        else:
            # Weak correlation: any rating with slight bias toward base
            options = list(range(1, 6))
            weights = [0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30, 0.25] if base >= 4 else \
                     [0.25, 0.30, 0.20, 0.15, 0.10] if base <= 2 else \
                     [0.15, 0.20, 0.30, 0.20, 0.15]
            return random.choices(options, weights=weights)[0]
    
    wait_time_rating = correlated_rating(overall_satisfaction, 0.5)
    staff_friendliness = correlated_rating(overall_satisfaction, 0.6)
    facility_cleanliness = correlated_rating(overall_satisfaction, 0.4)
    care_quality_rating = correlated_rating(overall_satisfaction, 0.7)
    communication_clarity = correlated_rating(overall_satisfaction, 0.6)
    
    # Would recommend based on overall satisfaction
    if overall_satisfaction >= 4:
        would_recommend = random.random() < 0.85
    elif overall_satisfaction == 3:
        would_recommend = random.random() < 0.40
    else:
        would_recommend = random.random() < 0.10
    
    # Generate feedback based on overall satisfaction
    doctor_name = customer_name.split()[-1]  # Use last name as doctor reference
    aspect = random.choice(aspects)
    
    if overall_satisfaction >= 4:
        patient_feedback = random.choice(positive_feedback)
    elif overall_satisfaction == 3:
        patient_feedback = random.choice(neutral_feedback)
    else:
        patient_feedback = random.choice(negative_feedback)
    
    if patient_feedback:
        patient_feedback = patient_feedback.format(name=doctor_name, aspect=aspect)
    
    # Response time: faster for negative feedback
    if overall_satisfaction <= 2:
        response_time_days = random.randint(1, 5)
    elif overall_satisfaction == 3:
        response_time_days = random.randint(3, 9)
    else:
        response_time_days = random.randint(4, 14)
    
    survey_method = random.choices(survey_methods, weights=survey_method_weights)[0]
    
    new_surveys.append((
        survey_id,
        order_id,
        survey_date,
        overall_satisfaction,
        wait_time_rating,
        staff_friendliness,
        facility_cleanliness,
        care_quality_rating,
        would_recommend,
        communication_clarity,
        appointment_scheduling_ease,
        patient_feedback,
        response_time_days,
        survey_method
    ))

# Insert new survey records
cur.executemany("""
    INSERT INTO demo.patient_satisfaction (
        survey_id, order_id, survey_date, overall_satisfaction,
        wait_time_rating, staff_friendliness, facility_cleanliness,
        care_quality_rating, would_recommend, communication_clarity,
        appointment_scheduling_ease, patient_feedback, response_time_days,
        survey_method
    ) VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s)
""", new_surveys)

print(f"Added {len(new_surveys)} new patient satisfaction surveys")
print(f"Total surveys now: {len(existing_survey_orders) + len(new_surveys)}")
